newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move lower in mid-week.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move lower in mid-week.

text.p: Cyprus's stocks moved lower in mid-week trading on Wednesday at prices described as "humiliatingly low" by a leading businessman.
"The prices are at very low levels," said Nikos Shakolas, chairman of NKS Holdings which has five companies listed on the 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE).
"Large investors should not try to influence the market to create an artificial high, it has to do it on its own ... but these prices are humiliatingly low," he said.
The CSE all-share index closed at 83.55 points, shedding 1.20 points, or 1.42 percent, from Friday's closing figure of 84.75.

Shakolas was speaking at a news conference to announce a reshuffle in life and general insurance portfolios of Paneuropean Insurance, Philiki Insurance and Interamerican Insurance. He did not give any reason for the share drop.
"The prices should be higher... I would not recommend any investor to sell, and brokers should not sell at such low prices," he told the audience, which included floor traders.

The CSE has been moving in negative territory for more than a week amid renewed tension on the divided island sparked last week by the discovery of a Turkish Cypriot sentry found dead at his post close to the ceasefire line 10 days ago.
The island was also swept with rumours, later dismissed by the government, of an attack on military positions by Turkish forces.
Banking stocks, which represent the bulk of transactions on the CSE closed lower. The banking sub index closed at 89.88 points, dropping 1.66 points or 1.81 percent from Friday's close of 91.54.
Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed lower at 338.5, shedding nine cents from Friday's close of 347.5. The Cyprus Popular Bank, lost 2.5 cents, to close at 320.5 from Friday's close of 323.
On Tuesday the Popular Bank released its six monthly results showing an increase in pre-tax profit of 13.2 percent to 18.20 million pounds ($39.5 million) compared to 16.08 million last year.
The Hellenic Bank HBCP.CY closed at 253.5 from Friday's close of 257.5.
By contrast, the sub index of insurance companies made gains, closing on Wednesday at 63.13 from 61.62 on Friday. ($=0.46 pounds)
